synthetic_episode.teaching_objective: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction from ischemic cardiomyopathy in a 66-year-old Native Hawaiian man, sheriff of Honolulu and a lifelong Olympic swimmer and surfer, five years after a heart attack. The episode covers breathlessness, ankle swelling and tiredness diagnosed by NT-proBNP and echocardiography (ejection fraction 30%); invasive coronary angiography for the ischemic cause; the four pillars of guideline-directed medical therapy under the 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA guideline and the 2024 ACC decision pathway: changing lisinopril to sacubitril-valsartan with a 36-hour washout, changing metoprolol tartrate to carvedilol, empagliflozin and spironolactone, titrated every two weeks with potassium, magnesium and kidney checks; a loop diuretic adjusted to euvolemia; intravenous iron for iron deficiency; sick-day rules when vomiting and diarrhea raise potassium and creatinine; a missed laboratory check recorded honestly; the decision against a primary-prevention defibrillator when the ejection fraction rose from 30% to 38% after more than 90 days of therapy; sodium guidance without routine fluid restriction; cardiac rehabilitation adapted to an ocean athlete, with swimming and surfing safety; vaccinations; and culturally safe care for a Native Hawaiian patient, with his ʻohana involved as he chooses, his own healing practices respected, and attention to the higher and earlier burden of heart failure hospitalization among Native Hawaiians.

visit_schedule.purpose: Establishing care for six weeks of breathlessness, ankle swelling and tiredness five years after a heart attack: examination, ECG, chest X-ray, NT-proBNP and laboratory tests, a diuretic, and the plan for an echocardiogram
Two-week review: echocardiogram, heart failure cardiology consultation the same day, the diagnosis, and guideline-directed medicines
Two-week review after sacubitril-valsartan, carvedilol and empagliflozin: kidney function, potassium, angiography result and the next medicine
Same-day sick visit for vomiting and diarrhea on heart failure medicines
Two-week review, five days after the sick visit: kidney function and potassium, medicine doses, lipids, and cardiac rehabilitation adapted to the ocean
Six-month review: repeat echocardiogram after more than 90 days of therapy, the defibrillator decision, iron, the delayed titration step, and plans for the year

assessment.assessment: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, stage C, NYHA class III, from ischemic cardiomyopathy: an ejection fraction of 30% with a thinned, akinetic anterior wall and apex in the territory of the old anterior infarction, and Q waves to match. The mitral regurgitation is functional, from the dilated ventricle. TSH and blood count exclude thyroid disease and anemia as contributors; he does not drink alcohol

Invasive coronary angiography is reasonable in new HFrEF with a likely coronary cause, to define the anatomy and look for disease that revascularization could help, especially in vessels other than the infarct artery. A thinned, akinetic wall of 5 mm or less is unlikely to recover even if its artery is opened

Start all four classes within weeks rather than months. Stop lisinopril and begin sacubitril-valsartan 24/26 mg twice daily at least 36 hours after the last lisinopril dose, to avoid angioedema. Replace metoprolol tartrate, which is not one of the beta-blockers proven in heart failure, with carvedilol 3.125 mg twice daily. Start empagliflozin 10 mg now. Add spironolactone 12.5 mg at the next visit if potassium is below 5.0 mmol/L and eGFR above 30. Then raise one medicine every two weeks toward target doses (sacubitril-valsartan 97/103 mg and carvedilol 25 mg twice daily) as blood pressure, heart rate, potassium and kidney function allow, with a metabolic panel one to two weeks after each change. Keep furosemide at the lowest dose that keeps him dry. Teach sick-day rules

Ferritin below 100 ng/mL is iron deficiency in heart failure even without anemia. Intravenous iron improves symptoms, exercise capacity and quality of life; oral iron does not. Give ferric carboxymaltose 750 mg today and again in two weeks, and check iron studies at about six months

Not now. Repeat the echocardiogram after at least 90 days of optimized therapy; a primary-prevention ICD is indicated if the ejection fraction is still 35% or below with NYHA class II to III and a good expected survival. His QRS of 104 ms does not meet criteria for resynchronization

Exercise training is safe and helps in stable HFrEF. Cardiac rehabilitation for heart failure is covered once he has had six weeks of stable therapy and no procedure in the previous six weeks. Until then, walking. After rehabilitation, swimming is reasonable in calm water with a companion; breath-hold diving and big surf should wait until he is clearly stable, because a sudden loss of consciousness in the water is the main danger. Drink water through the morning on the diuretic and empagliflozin
